description: Organized team chat. The server is Python and Django, with a JavaScript web app.
contribution_notes: Zulip keeps a large set of issues marked for new contributors and documents how to run the development server. Docs, UI copy, and small Django fixes are realistic first changes.

description: A small Python web framework for HTTP applications.
contribution_notes: Docs, examples, and focused bug fixes are the usual way in. The codebase stays small enough to read in an afternoon.

description: A Python web framework for database-backed sites, with its own ORM, admin, and auth.
contribution_notes: Django tags easy tickets. Documentation and tests are accepted paths before changing the ORM or request stack.

description: A Python framework for building HTTP APIs with type hints.
contribution_notes: Many open issues are docs, examples, and small API clarifications. A person who has shipped a FastAPI service can start there.

description: A Python HTTP client with a small, widely used API.
contribution_notes: Fixes tend to be narrow: docs, tests, and edge cases in how requests are prepared and sent.

description: The Python test runner most projects use for unit and integration tests.
contribution_notes: People who write tests for a living can help with plugin docs, assertion messages, and small runner bugs.

description: Python data structures and tools for tables, time series, and file formats.
contribution_notes: New contributors usually start with documentation, tests, or a single method in the DataFrame API.

description: Array computing for Python, used underneath most scientific libraries.
contribution_notes: Docs and Python-side tests are approachable. Changes in the C core suit someone who already works with numerical code.

description: Classical machine learning in Python: models, metrics, and preprocessing.
contribution_notes: The project documents a first-contribution path. Examples, docstrings, and estimator tests are common starting work.

description: Python plotting library for charts and figures.
contribution_notes: Gallery examples and documentation issues are a direct fit for someone who already makes charts.

description: Turn Python scripts into data apps with a small widget API.
contribution_notes: Docs, examples, and frontend widget polish are open to people who have built small data apps.

description: The Jupyter Notebook interface for running code, markdown, and plots in the browser.
contribution_notes: UI bugs and documentation suit someone who uses notebooks daily.

description: A Python HTTP client with sync and async APIs.
contribution_notes: Issues are often about HTTP edge cases. Comfort with async Python is the useful background.

description: SQL toolkit and ORM for Python.
contribution_notes: Documentation and dialect tests are the on-ramp. Core compiler changes need existing SQLAlchemy experience.

description: A Python library for command-line interfaces.
contribution_notes: Docs and small behavior bugs are a good match for someone who has built CLIs.

description: An extremely fast Python linter and formatter, written in Rust.
contribution_notes: New lint rules and docs are labeled for contributors. Rust experience helps, and Python rule ideas are still useful.

description: Model definitions and training utilities for language, vision, and audio models.
contribution_notes: Docs, examples, and model-card fixes are approachable. Architecture changes suit someone who has trained or fine-tuned models.

description: Tensor library and automatic differentiation system used to train neural networks.
contribution_notes: The project is large. Documentation, tests, and a single operator are more realistic than core dispatcher work unless the person already writes PyTorch extensions.

description: A platform for authoring and scheduling data pipelines.
contribution_notes: Provider docs and small operator fixes are a fit for someone who has run data jobs.

description: A data exploration and charting application. Flask on the server, React in the browser.
contribution_notes: Chart docs, frontend polish, and SQL lab bugs match a mix of Python and React experience.

description: A JavaScript library for building user interfaces from components.
contribution_notes: The website and docs accept contributions from people who use React. Compiler and reconciler changes need deeper runtime experience.

description: The Vue 3 framework for building component-based interfaces.
contribution_notes: Docs and small reactivity bugs are the on-ramp for someone who has shipped Vue apps.

description: A compiler that turns component files into small JavaScript UI code.
contribution_notes: Documentation and compiler tests are approachable for someone who has built with Svelte.

description: A React framework for server-rendered and static web applications.
contribution_notes: Docs and examples move quickly. A person who has deployed a Next.js app can start with those before touching the compiler.

description: Frontend tooling: a dev server and production bundler for JavaScript projects.
contribution_notes: Docs, plugin examples, and small dev-server bugs suit someone who already uses Vite.

description: A minimal Node.js framework for HTTP servers.
contribution_notes: The code is small. Docs and middleware examples are a realistic first patch for someone who has written Express routes.

description: An opinionated formatter for JavaScript, TypeScript, and related languages.
contribution_notes: Many issues are formatting edge cases with a failing fixture. That is a good match for someone who uses Prettier every day.

description: A pluggable linter for JavaScript.
contribution_notes: New rules and docs are labeled for contributors who already configure ESLint.

description: A utility-first CSS framework.
contribution_notes: Documentation fixes are the common first contribution for people who build interfaces with Tailwind.

description: Browser automation for end-to-end tests in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit.
contribution_notes: Docs and test examples are a fit for someone who has written browser tests.

description: A workshop for building UI components in isolation.
contribution_notes: Docs, examples, and addon bugs match frontend developers who already use Storybook.

description: A JavaScript 3D library built on WebGL.
contribution_notes: Examples and docs are the usual start. Renderer internals suit someone who has already shipped a Three.js scene.

description: JavaScript tools for binding data to documents and drawing charts.
contribution_notes: Documentation and examples are the right scale for someone who has built charts with D3.

description: A web framework for content-heavy sites, with islands of client-side JavaScript.
contribution_notes: Docs and examples are active. Someone who has published an Astro site can fix those without learning the compiler first.

description: A TypeScript ORM and database toolkit.
contribution_notes: Docs and client examples are approachable. Query-engine work is for people already deep in databases.

description: The Node.js JavaScript runtime.
contribution_notes: Documentation is the realistic first patch. Core C++ changes need existing runtime experience.

description: A JavaScript and TypeScript runtime written in Rust.
contribution_notes: Docs and the standard library are more approachable than the runtime core. Rust experience matters for most code changes.

description: An HTTP web framework for Go.
contribution_notes: Docs, examples, and small middleware fixes suit someone who has written Go HTTP handlers.

description: The official GitHub command-line tool, written in Go.
contribution_notes: The project labels help-wanted issues. Someone who uses `gh` and writes Go can pick up a command bug.

description: A static site generator written in Go.
contribution_notes: Docs and template bugs are a fit for people who already publish sites with Hugo.

description: The Go programming language and its standard library.
contribution_notes: The wiki explains how to send a change. Small standard-library docs and tests are more realistic than compiler work.

description: Open-source infrastructure as code. A fork of Terraform under a FOSS license.
contribution_notes: Docs and provider examples match people who already write infrastructure code.

description: Monitoring system and time-series database, written in Go.
contribution_notes: Documentation and exporter-adjacent bugs are the start. Query-engine work needs existing Prometheus experience.

description: Dashboards and alerting for metrics, logs, and traces. Go backend, TypeScript frontend.
contribution_notes: Panel docs and frontend bugs are approachable for someone who has built Grafana dashboards.

description: A line-oriented search tool written in Rust.
contribution_notes: The tool is finished and careful. Docs and narrow search bugs suit someone who already writes Rust CLIs.

description: The async runtime most Rust network services use.
contribution_notes: Docs and examples are the on-ramp. Scheduler changes need existing async Rust experience.

description: The Rust programming language, compiler, and standard library.
contribution_notes: The compiler labels easy issues, but most of them still assume you can build Rust from source. Docs and error-message fixes are the usual start.

description: A framework for production-ready Java and Kotlin services.
contribution_notes: Documentation and samples are the realistic first contribution for someone who has built Spring Boot services.

description: A UI toolkit for mobile, web, and desktop apps, using Dart.
contribution_notes: Docs and framework examples are labeled for new contributors who have shipped a Flutter app.

description: A game engine. The editor and runtime are C++, with GDScript for games.
contribution_notes: The engine tags junior jobs. Docs, editor usability, and GDScript demos are a better start than the renderer.

description: Computer vision and image processing, with C++ and Python APIs.
contribution_notes: Python samples and docs are approachable. Algorithm changes suit someone who already uses OpenCV.

description: A source-code editor built with TypeScript and Electron.
contribution_notes: The wiki explains how to build the editor. Extension-host docs and small workbench bugs are a fit for daily VS Code users who write TypeScript.

description: A framework for desktop apps using JavaScript, HTML, and CSS.
contribution_notes: Docs and small API fixes are approachable. Chromium upgrades are not a first task.

description: A package manager for macOS and Linux, written in Ruby.
contribution_notes: Formulae, docs, and small Ruby fixes are a common first contribution for people who use Homebrew.

description: A Ruby web framework with routing, an ORM, and server-rendered views.
contribution_notes: Rails marks issues for new contributors. Guides and small Active Record fixes match people who have built a Rails app.

description: Customer support chat. Ruby on Rails on the server, Vue in the browser.
contribution_notes: The project labels good first issues across the Rails API and the Vue inbox.

description: The Laravel PHP framework for web applications.
contribution_notes: Docs and small framework bugs are a fit for someone who has shipped a Laravel app.

description: The source of MDN Web Docs for HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
contribution_notes: Writing and correcting docs is the work. Strong web-platform knowledge matters more than a large codebase.

description: The Kubernetes documentation site.
contribution_notes: Localization and doc fixes are the intended first contribution for people who use Kubernetes.

description: A free coding curriculum and its learning platform.
contribution_notes: Curriculum lessons and UI copy are written so a first contribution can be a single lesson or a small bug.

description: A collection of Python algorithms with explanations and tests.
contribution_notes: Adding a well-tested algorithm or fixing an explanation is a contained first change.

description: A curated directory of free APIs.
contribution_notes: Entries are small markdown edits. Useful when the resume shows API work and the person wants a first merged pull request.

description: IT automation in Python: playbooks, modules, and inventory.
contribution_notes: Module docs and small bug fixes match people who already write playbooks.

description: A community configuration and plugin set for the Zsh shell.
contribution_notes: Plugins and docs are small shell scripts. A good fit for someone who lives in the terminal.

description: A PDF reader built with JavaScript.
contribution_notes: Viewer UI bugs and docs are more approachable than the PDF parser.

description: An open-source backend in a single binary: database, auth, and a dashboard. Written in Go.
contribution_notes: Dashboard polish and docs suit someone who has used PocketBase as a backend.

description: A Postgres development platform: auth, storage, and auto-generated APIs.
contribution_notes: Docs and studio UI issues are a fit for people who have built on Supabase.

description: A backend server for web and mobile apps, with auth, databases, and storage.
contribution_notes: Docs and SDK examples are the usual start for someone who has integrated Appwrite.

description: A headless CMS built with JavaScript.
contribution_notes: Admin UI bugs and docs are approachable for someone who has modeled content in Strapi.

description: An open-source spreadsheet interface on top of relational databases.
contribution_notes: UI and docs issues are a match for people who have used NocoDB with Postgres or MySQL.

description: Open-source scheduling. A Next.js application with a Prisma database.
contribution_notes: The product is a full Next.js app. UI bugs and booking-flow docs suit someone who has built similar applications.

description: A document archive. Django, a consumer for OCR, and a web UI.
contribution_notes: Docs and small Django or UI fixes match someone who self-hosts the app or has built Django sites.

description: A self-hosted photo and video backup service. The server and apps are TypeScript.
contribution_notes: Mobile and web UI issues are labeled for contributors who use the product.

description: Team chat. A Go server and a React web app.
contribution_notes: Help-wanted issues span the Go API and the React client. Web UI bugs are the smaller starting point.

description: The Git version-control system, written in C.
contribution_notes: Documentation and tests are the published on-ramp. The mailing-list workflow is part of the contribution, and C experience matters.

description: The PostgreSQL relational database, written in C.
contribution_notes: Docs are reviewed on the mailing lists. Code changes assume you already know Postgres internals or are willing to read a subsystem carefully.

description: The Linux kernel. The GitHub repository is a read-only mirror of a project developed by email.
contribution_notes: torvalds/linux does not accept GitHub pull requests. Patches go by email to the subsystem mailing lists, following Documentation/process/submitting-patches.rst. This is a large C codebase; a first change is usually a small, reviewed fix in one subsystem.

description: A free CFD toolbox from the OpenFOAM Foundation. The GitHub repository is a mirror, not the place where changes are merged.
contribution_notes: OpenFOAM/OpenFOAM-dev does not take GitHub pull requests. The OpenFOAM Foundation reviews contributions through its own process and bug tracker. The ESI edition is developed separately on develop.openfoam.com. Expect a large C++ numerical codebase.

description: A podcast manager for Android.
contribution_notes: Search open and closed issues before filing a bug, and include the device, Android version, AntennaPod version, and steps to reproduce. Code changes are pull requests.

description: Thunderbird for Android, an email app. The project was formerly K-9 Mail.
contribution_notes: The contributing guide covers reporting bugs, finding an issue, setting up a development environment, and opening a pull request.

description: The official WordPress app for iOS.
contribution_notes: Bugs, questions, and feature requests are GitHub issues with a title prefix such as Bug: or Feature Request:. Translations are managed in GlotPress. A code of conduct applies to everyone who participates.

description: Software for live streaming and screen recording.
contribution_notes: Changes are public pull requests with a written description and motivation. Project members decide what is merged, and the guide asks contributors to weigh scope and maintainability.

description: A Vim fork focused on extensibility and usability.
contribution_notes: Read the dev quickstart and the AI-assisted work section before opening a pull request. Issues labeled complexity:low are a starting point. Vimscript runtime files are mostly maintained by Vim; Lua files are maintained by Neovim.

description: An analytical database system for fast local queries.
contribution_notes: Search existing issues before reporting a bug, and include a code sample or test that shows the problem. A bugfix patch should add a unit test when that is possible.

description: A free, cross-platform geographical information system.
contribution_notes: Bug reports and fixes go to the GitHub issue tracker. A code change is a fork, a pre-commit hook (version 4.1 or newer), and a pull request. The developer guide on docs.qgis.org covers the process and tests.

description: A scalable real-time operating system for multiple hardware architectures.
contribution_notes: Patches are submitted to the project. Zephyr is Apache 2.0 and follows the Developer Certificate of Origin. The in-repo file points at the full contribution guide on docs.zephyrproject.org.

description: The server and API for the Jellyfin media system.
contribution_notes: The repository contributing file points to the Jellyfin documentation at jellyfin.org for how to help, including code contributions.

description: A cross-platform shell and scripting language.
contribution_notes: Documentation, issues, and code are all listed ways to contribute. Docs for an existing cmdlet start in MicrosoftDocs/PowerShell-Docs, which the guide calls a low-friction first step.

description: A data-driven game engine written in Rust.
contribution_notes: Start with the contribute introduction and the AI usage policy on bevy.org. The repository contributing file links there before code changes.

description: A high-performance, multiplayer code editor.
contribution_notes: Keep at most three pull requests open. Discuss a feature in a GitHub discussion and get staff confirmation before writing the code, especially for the extension API.

description: A browser engine meant for embedding web technology in applications.
contribution_notes: The repository contributing file points to the Servo book at book.servo.org for how to get started. Code changes are still pull requests.

description: A Python library of scientific algorithms, built with NumPy.
contribution_notes: Pull requests are welcome. The guide asks for unit tests, documentation, and code style, and for contributed code to be under SciPy's license. Details are in the developer hacking guide.

description: An implementation of the Grammar of Graphics in R.
contribution_notes: Issues need a minimal reproducible example: packages, data, and code. Changes are suggested with a pull request. A contributor code of conduct applies.

description: The Julia programming language.
contribution_notes: New contributors are pointed at a walkthrough for a first Julia pull request. If a pull request includes substantive generative-AI output, the guide asks you to disclose that and review the changes. Community standards apply.

description: The core of ZAP, an open-source web application security scanner.
contribution_notes: Usage questions start with the FAQ, the user guide, or the zaproxy-users group. Bugs are GitHub issues. The full contributing guide is on zaproxy.org.

description: Identity and access management for applications and services.
contribution_notes: Open a discussion before a large change. Smaller changes can go straight to a pull request. How to build the codebase is documented in the building guide.

description: Home automation that keeps control of devices local.
contribution_notes: Documentation help happens on home-assistant.io. Code changes are a fork and a pull request against the dev branch, with tests. Integrating a device that is not supported yet is a common kind of change.

description: The Nextcloud server, for self-hosted files and collaboration.
contribution_notes: Install and usage questions belong on the forum. Bug reports should use the issue templates after a search, and this repository is the server rather than the apps. Code changes are pull requests.

description: A self-hosted microblogging server that federates with other servers.
contribution_notes: The guide lists bug reports, translations, code, and documentation. An API change also needs a pull request on the documentation repository. Read the development guide and the AI contribution policy before sending code.

description: The block editor project for WordPress.
contribution_notes: The contributor handbook covers code, design, documentation, and issue triage. Setup for code changes is in the handbook's developer section.

description: A virtual whiteboard for sketching hand-drawn diagrams.
contribution_notes: The repository contributing file sends you to the Excalidraw docs for how to contribute.

description: A browser editor for OpenStreetMap.
contribution_notes: A code of conduct applies. Translations are managed on Transifex, and you do not need to know programming to help. Code changes are pull requests.

description: Run and serve large language models on your own machine.
contribution_notes: Local build steps are in docs/development.md. The guide points at open bug and performance issues. Security vulnerabilities must not be disclosed in public issues; see SECURITY.md.
